description: Part single, part double storey rear extension, two storey front extension, rear dormer extension, and alterations to fenestration
decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be commenced not later than three years from the date of this permission.
Reason:-
To comply with the requirements of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004).
All new external finishes shall be carried out in materials to match those of the existing building(s) to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason:-
To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.
The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out otherwise than in complete accordance with the approved plans (as set out on page one of this decision notice).
Reason:-
For the avoidance of doubt and to ensure that the development is carried out as approved.

The proposed glazing within the flank door adjacent to No.92 Wingletye Lane as shown on drawing nos. WL:90a:JAWS:10B, WL:90a:JAWS:11B & WL:90a:JAWS:14B shall be permanently glazed with obscure glass not less than level 4 on the standard scale of obscurity and shall thereafter be maintained.
Reason:-
In the interests of privacy.

The proposed first floor flank and loft windows serving the landing and en-suite as shown on drawing nos. WL:90a:JAWS:9B & WL:90a:JAWS:14B shall be permanently glazed with obscure glass not less than 4 on the standard scale of obscurity and shall thereafter be maintained and permanently fixed shut.
Reason:-
In the interests of privacy.

The roof light within the roof of the two storey front extension as shown drawing nos. WL:90a:JAWS:14B shall be  obscure-glazed, and  non-opening unless the parts of the window which can be opened are more than 1.7m above the floor of the room in which the window is installed.
Reason - In the interest of privacy and to protect the amenity of the adjacent neighbours

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015, no window or other opening (other than those shown on the submitted and approved plan,) shall be formed in the flank wall(s) of the building(s) hereby permitted, unless specific permission under the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 has first been sought and obtained in writing from the Local Planning Authority.
Reason:-
In order to ensure a satisfactory development that will not result in any loss of privacy or damage to the environment of neighbouring properties which exist or may be proposed in the future.

Notwithstanding the details shown on drawing nos. WL:90a:JAWS:14B, WL:90a:JAWS:15B & WL:90a:JAWS:16A accompanying the application, the face and cheeks of the rear dormer window shall be tile hung to match the appearance of the roof of the existing dwelling unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason:-
To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area, and in order that the development accords with Policy 26 of the Havering Local Plan.

Statement Required by Article 35 (2) of the Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015: In accordance with paragraph 38 of the National Planning Policy Framework, improvements required to make the proposal acceptable were negotiated with Mr Wallington-Smith (Agent) by phone and e-mail. The revision involved reducing the depth of the ground floor rear and setting the first floor further away from the boundary and marginally increasing the depth. The amendments were subsequently submitted on 08/12/25, 11/12/25 & 16/12/25.
